title: Unary ~ (Invert) does Python bitwise-not on booleans instead of Polars logical-not (~True shown as -2)
description: _unaryop maps ast.Invert to `return ~val`. For boolean inputs this is Python bitwise complement: `~True == -2`, `~False == -1`. But in Polars `~pl.col('mask')` on a Boolean column is LOGICAL negation (`~True -> False`, `~False -> True`), and `~pl.col('flag')` is one of the most common Polars idioms for negating a predicate/mask. The evaluator therefore displays a meaningless signed integer (-1/-2) as the computed value for a negated boolean in the trace waterfall, instead of the boolean Polars actually produces. This null/bool divergence is not one of the broad categories the catalog enumerates (the replace finding lists null-propagation / branch-selection / string-coercion / aggregation; unary boolean ~ is none of these) and is far more commonly hit than the horizontal-func edge cases already catalogued.
evidence: Executed repro (polars 1.39.2). Code: out=~pl.col('flag'). flag=True -> evaluator result_value=-2, real Polars=False. flag=False -> evaluator=-1, real Polars=True. The AST for ~pl.col('flag') is UnaryOp(op=Invert), routed to line 1647-1648 which returns ~True == -2.
